battle.name: 三八年戰爭
battle.brief: 稱德天皇即位後，陸奧與岩城防備線出現裂痕；773年多賀城高階軍官唐居狩野阿麻羅叛離，774年毛野城陷落，戰爭全面爆發。朝廷自坂東調集大軍反攻，石城部阿多留威於諏訪之關一度擊敗朝廷軍，至811年大局平定。本卡羅馬短劍非本役制式裝備，其刺擊型短兵的功能由和風大刀與短刀擔任。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 三八年戰爭（又稱三十八年戰爭）自770年起、至811年方告平息，交戰雙方是平安朝朝廷與東北地方的蝦夷諸部。朝廷一方以天皇為最高統帥，實際的軍令集中於征夷大將軍一職，該職自天平寶字二年起固定由公卿或藤原、大伴、中臣諸氏擔當，並常加「征東大將軍」別號，用以經略陸奧、出羽、岩城；出兵的組成包括朝廷直屬的兵糧兵、來自關東（坂東）與越前、伊勢、尾張的徵發兵，以及坂上、紀、巨萬、秦等豪族所出的部族私兵，前線屯兵以陸奧國府多賀城與陸奧、岩城沿線的柵、館、鎮為骨幹。蝦夷一方並非單一國家，而是分據陸奧、出羽、岩城、越後的部族聯盟，以「部」為單位、由首領直轄，首領層以石城部、志波部、桃生部最為強勢；原為朝廷軍官的唐居狩野阿麻羅在773年倒戈，直接引爆戰事。朝廷在東北依賴通曉「夷言」的通譯傳話，實行羈縻、給姓、編戶與俘囚安置並用，把對方首領吸收進官僚體系，這是整場戰爭得以長期進行的制度前提。
countriesEn: The Thirty-Eight Years' War, which opened in 770 and did not die down until 811, was fought between the court of the Heian dynasty at Kyoto and the Emishi tribes of northeastern Japan. On the court side the supreme command remained with the emperor, but the real military directive lay with the office of the chōei taishōgun, Conqueror-General of the Emishi, a post fixed from the Hōki era among the nobles of the Fujiwara, Ōtomo and Nakatsukasa houses and often carrying the additional title of chōtō taishōgun for the administration of Mutsu, Dewa and Iwate. The troops raised for it combined court-controlled levies and food-service conscripts, contingents mustered from Kantō in the east, as well as from Echizen, Ise and Owari, and the private war-bands of the Sakanoue, Ki, Ōmi and Hata lineages; on the frontier the backbone was the chain of saku fences, yakata stations and fortified posts running from Taga Castle, the provincial capital of Mutsu, along the northern mountains. The Emishi side was not a single state but a loose confederation of tribes spread over Mutsu, Dewa, Iwate and Echigo, each part divided into units and commanded directly by its own chief, with the Isawa, Shiwa and Momuse groups the most powerful; a high-ranking Emishi officer in imperial service, Korehari no Azamaro, defected in 773 and set the whole conflict ablaze. In the north the court relied on interpreters who spoke the barbarian tongue, and governed through a mixture of loose rein, the granting of surnames, enrolment in the provincial districts and the keeping of hostages; the absorption of enemy chiefs into the bureaucratic order was the institutional precondition that allowed this war to run for nearly four decades.
people: 朝政方面，戰爭始於稱德天皇即位（770年）的混亂期，藤原不比等這位北家領袖在772年病逝，朝廷在東北的人事與後勤一時找不到主腦，防守線出現空隙；此後藤原一族仍以比等之子孫與大伴氏爭奪征夷大將軍的寶座。戰場上的關鍵人物包括：接掌軍令的大伴弟麻呂；以騎射對付游擊而聞名、797年出任征夷大將軍的坂上田村麻呂，他在802年迫使石城部首領阿多留威降伏，並主持經營多賀城；紀氏將領紀小麻呂在789年率軍北進時於衣川、諏訪之關遭石城部奇襲而大敗，紀廣純等將士陣歿，渡北上川時大量兵力溺死。後來桓武天皇、嵯峨天皇以兩代天皇的名義持續投入兵員，並在784年遷都長岡京、794年遷都平安京，把首都的防線往後拉。蝦夷方面，唐居狩野阿麻羅是第一個公開叛離的朝廷軍官，阿多留威與モレ是石城部的主要首領，其後還有Morokuri、Otoshiro、Yasoshima、Isaseko、Ikako等部族首領在記錄中陸續出現；降附朝廷的百濟王族百濟王興達等北方協力者，則在外交與招撫上扮演穿針引線的角色。
peopleEn: At the level of government the war broke out amid the confusion following the accession of Emperor Kōnin in 770. Fujiwara no Fuhito, head of the northern branch of the Fujiwara, died of illness in 772, and the court's arrangements for personnel and supply in the north suddenly lost a director, leaving gaps in the defensive line; the Fujiwara and the Ōtomo houses went on contesting the post of the chōei taishōgun for the following decades. The key figures on the battlefield include Ōtomo no Otomaro, who carried the army's directive; Sakanoue no Tamuramaro, famous for using horse archery against the Emishi raiders, who took office as chōei taishōgun in 797, forced the Isawa chief Aterui to surrender in 802 and directed the consolidation of Taga Castle; and the commander of the Ki house, Ki no Kosami, whose army was ambushed and badly beaten by the Isawa at the Koromo river and the pass of Sufuse in 789, where officers such as Ki no Hirozumi were killed and a large part of the imperial force drowned while fording the Kitakami. The emperors themselves kept committing men: Emperor Kanmu and Emperor Saga carried the war through two reigns, and the court moved the capital first to Nagaoka in 784 and then to Heian-kyō in 794, pulling the seat of government back from the northern threat. On the Emishi side Korehari no Azamaro was the first senior officer to break with the court; Aterui and More were the leading Isawa chiefs, and the chronicles go on to name further leaders such as Morokuri, Otoshiro, Yasoshima, Isaseko and Ikako. Collaborators from the north who submitted to the court, including the Kudara prince Konikishi Shuntetsu, acted as go-betweens in diplomacy and in persuading tribes to come in.
kits: 本卡兵器為羅馬短劍（Gladius），公元前100年前後已定型：雙刃、直脊、圓盤形護手，刃長約半米出頭，設計重點是刺而不是砍，短兵相接時靠盾緣與對手的破綻完成刺突。它並不是三八年戰爭的制式裝備，本役中與之功能對位的，是和風的鐵製大刀（太刀）與短刀：這類單刃刀承襲自大陸的直刃刀傳統，在東北的考古出土品中屢見，例如宮城縣丸森町子鳥子遺跡出土的鐵刀與馬具、多賀城跡出土的鐵刀、岩手縣一關市志波古城跡出土的兵器殘件，都顯示當時蝦夷與朝廷雙方都已能自產鐵器。弓矢是本役的實際主力：朝廷以大弓配石突矢、楔矢，蝦夷同樣用弓，並以鐵鏃取代石鏃；防具方面朝廷使用頭冑、草摺、胴丸、籠手、脛當與木製楯，蝦夷多以皮革與木札甲禦寒風，騎兵則配鞍、鐙、轡與韁繩。攻守器材方面，柵、塀、館、城形成沿北上川與奧羽山脈的縱深防線，海路則以舟船向陸奧灣輸送兵員與糧秣。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Roman gladius, a type already established around 100 BC: double-edged, with a straight spine and a disc-shaped guard, a little over half a metre of blade, designed for the thrust rather than the cut, and used in close combat by working around the rim of the shield and the gaps of the enemy. It was not a standard issue arm in the Thirty-Eight Years' War; its functional counterpart in this campaign was the Japanese iron tachi and short sword, single-edged blades that continue the continental straight-sword tradition, and the archaeological record from the north shows both sides working their own iron: iron swords and harness from the Konezako site in Marumori, Miyagi, iron swords from the Taga Castle site, and weapon fragments from the Shiwa Castle site at Ichinoseki in Iwate all attest to the same. The bow was the real workhorse of the war: the court used large bows with stone-tipped and wedge-shaped arrows, and the Emishi used bows as well, replacing stone points with iron ones. On the defensive side the court equipped men with head helmets, straw-armoured sleeves, dō-maru cuirasses, forearm guards and shin armour, together with wooden shields, while the Emishi relied more on leather and slatted wood against the winter cold; their horsemen carried saddles, stirrups, bridles and reins. For attack and defence, the frontier was structured as a chain of saku fences, yakata walls, stations and castles, and men and grain were moved to Mutsu Bay by boat.
tactics: 蝦夷的戰法以守城加游擊為骨幹：據點沿東往西的防備線串聯，多賀城、毛野城、志波城一類的城柵是其支撐，一旦某點失守便退入山地，避開朝廷大軍的正面與遠程優勢；騎兵在奧羽山區的谷道與河曲地帶反覆襲擊，尤其善用冬季結冰或淺灘可涉的河段，出其不意地切斷渡河中的縱隊。朝廷則以集大軍、分路進、步步為營應對：先在關東與中京徵集以萬計的兵力，再以多賀城、志波城等為前進基地，步步修築柵與塀，強迫蝦夷在不利於游擊的正面交鋒；坂上田村麻呂更把受過騎射訓練的兵卒大量投入，以弓騎壓制對方騎兵，使蝦夷失去機動優勢。戰術調整同樣重要：794年部分志波部首領改為朝廷盟友，其中以石城國的伊澤君大荒安日子最為關鍵，等於從聯盟內部抽走一塊，孤立石城部聯盟；802年阿多留威降附後，朝廷改以招撫、編戶、俘囚安置為主，殘餘的零星衝突一直延續到811年。補給線是雙方的共同弱點：自京都到多賀城陸路逾一千公里，關東與越前前線的糧秣多靠粟、稗與海運，一旦存糧不足，遠征軍就會被迫冬季撤回，甚至在回程中遭逢打劫。
tacticsEn: Emishi tactics rested on holding strongpoints and raiding. Their positions were strung along a defensive line running from east to west, supported by castles such as Taga, Monou and Shiwa; when a point fell they withdrew into the mountains rather than face the imperial mass and its long reach, and their horsemen struck repeatedly from valleys and river bends in the Ōu ranges, exploiting frozen rivers and shallow fords to cut columns caught mid-crossing. The court answered by massing, dividing the advance and fighting forward step by step: it mustered tens of thousands in Kantō and the capital region, used Taga and Shiwa as forward bases, built saku and yakata as it went, and forced the Emishi to meet them on ground unfavourable to raiding. Sakanoue no Tamuramaro committed large numbers of men trained in horse archery to suppress the Emishi horse, cancelling the advantage of mobility. Tactical adjustment mattered as much: in 794 a number of Shiwa chiefs, among them the Isawa no kimi Anushiko, switched to the court's side, tearing a piece out of the confederation and isolating the Isawa; after Aterui's surrender in 802 the court shifted to negotiation, enrolment and hostage-taking, with scattered fighting continuing until 811. Supply was the common weakness of both sides: the land route from Kyoto to Taga exceeded a thousand kilometres, the grain for the eastern front was millet and barnyard millet moved by road and sea, and when the stores ran short an expeditionary army had to withdraw in winter, sometimes ambushed on the way back.
data: 關於兵員與時間，戰爭的起訖存在兩種算法：多數史料以770年稱德天皇即位、朝廷在東北的權力交接失序為起點，以811年零星衝突平息為終點，合計約三十八年；另有一套說法把全面開戰放在774年9月5日毛野城淪陷，收束放在812年。數字方面，朝廷每次出征的兵員以千為單位，最大一役可能達一萬至兩萬人；776年為討伐志波部一次出動兩萬餘人卻告失敗。蝦夷方面的總戰力至多約三千名戰士，同一戰場上同時投入的常在千人左右。789年衣川（諏訪之關）一役，朝廷軍約四千人正欲渡北上川，遭石城部阿多留威率約一千人襲擊，損失約千人，許多兵員並非戰死而是渡河時溺斃，此數見於《續日本紀》卷四十。距離上，自京都經美濃、越前、能登至多賀城的陸路逾一千公里，冬半年奧羽山脈積雪封山，軍書常以數旬形容調兵與進軍的耗時；多賀城、志波城、毛野城三處城柵之間的距離則是數十至數百公里級的邊境格鬥縱深。
dataEn: On dates and numbers there are two reckonings. Most accounts start the war in 770, with the accession of Kōnin and the breakdown of authority in the north, and end it in 811 when the last skirmishes die away, giving a span of about thirty-eight years; another reckoning puts the general outbreak at the fall of Monou on 5 September 774 and the conclusion in 812. On figures: each imperial expedition was measured in thousands, the largest contingents perhaps running to ten or twenty thousand men, and in 776 an army of more than twenty thousand was sent against the Shiwa and failed. The entire Emishi force was at most some three thousand warriors, of whom perhaps a thousand would be engaged at any one time. At the Koromo river and the pass of Sufuse in 789 a court army of about four thousand was crossing the Kitakami when a force of about a thousand under the Isawa chief Aterui fell on it; it lost around a thousand men, many of them drowned rather than killed in action, a figure recorded in volume 40 of the Shoku Nihongi. On distances: the road from Kyoto through Mino, Echizen and Noto to Taga runs beyond a thousand kilometres, and in the winter months the Ōu mountains are closed by snow, so military records describe the mustering and the march in terms of tens of days. The distances between the frontier strongpoints of Taga, Shiwa and Monou are a matter of tens to hundreds of kilometres, which set the depth of the border fighting.
cause: 戰爭並非單一事件引爆，而是朝廷在東北的經略與蝦夷自身的政治經濟變化長期累積的結果。背景之一是八世紀前半奈良朝的極盛已過，藤原不比等在772年病逝後，北家內部的南北兩派、以及藤原與大伴兩姓對北方軍權的爭奪同時進入最激烈的時候，兵馬與經費的調度一時失序；朝廷在陸奧與岩城修築代代累積的柵、館、鎮，靠近石城部一側的毛野城防線最為薄弱。直接導火線則是773年多賀城高階軍官唐居狩野阿麻羅倒戈：他把軍中的防禦部署與後方補給的虛實洩給蝦夷，後者隨即於774年9月5日攻下毛野城，反過來掃平東起至西的一整條防線。就蝦夷方面而言，奧羽山區的鐵礦、馬群與毛皮漁獲，決定了他們與大和朝廷爭的是交易控制權；朝廷對北方部落的貢賦徵發、俘囚的調集，以及攙入國郡的企圖，都被視為直接侵害。更深一層的原因是部族聯盟內部的權力競逐：石城部、志波部、桃生部彼此爭雄，首領阿多留威的野心與朝廷招撫帶來的分化，使任何一方都難以長期置身事外。
causeEn: The war was not lit by a single incident but by the accumulation of the court's northern policy and of political and economic change within the Emishi themselves. In the background, the peak of the Nara period in the first half of the eighth century had passed; after Fujiwara no Fuhito died in 772 the rivalry between the northern and southern wings of the Fujiwara, and between the Fujiwara and the Ōtomo houses for military authority in the north, reached its sharpest point at once, and the mustering of soldiers and money lost its ordering for a time. The line of saku, yakata and fortified posts that the court had built up over generations in Mutsu and Iwate was thinnest at the Monou end facing the Isawa. The immediate trigger was the defection in 773 of Korehari no Azamaro, a senior officer of Taga Castle, who passed on the disposition of the defences and the state of the rear-area supply; the Emishi duly took Monou on 5 September 774 and swept the whole defensive line from east to west. On the Emishi side, the iron ore, horse herds and fur and fish resources of the Ōu region meant that what they contested with the Yamato court was control of trade; the court's levy of tribute, the calling up of hostages and the attempt to enroll the tribes into provinces were all read as direct infringement. One layer deeper lay the internal contest among the tribes: the Isawa, Shiwa and Momuse groups vied with one another, and the ambition of the chief Aterui together with the divisions brought into the confederation by court policy meant that no party could stay out of it for long.
impact: 這場長達三十八年的邊境戰爭，結果是朝廷取得戰術上的勝利，卻付出制度與財政上的重價。直接後果是東北體制的重整：802年石城部首領降附後，朝廷在陸奧國府多賀城設鎮守、經營柵線，統一編制北方國郡，並把降附首領編入官僚序列、授予姓與位階，蝦夷諸部由獨立的部族聯盟逐步轉化為朝廷支配下的國郡住民；同時大量俘囚被送京作為人質與役夫，這批人的後代日後成為俘囚王與東北豪族的重要源頭之一。首都的位置也因這場戰爭而改變：784年桓武天皇遷都長岡京，被視為避開北方騎兵威脅的舉動，794年再遷平安京後，天然的山地屏障取代了原先近在咫尺的陸奧戰線。制度層面上，征夷大將軍與坂上田村麻呂開創的鎮守體制被確立，多賀城經營、邊境柵館體系與騎射戰術都成為此後三百年間日本北部國防的骨架。史籍方面，《續日本紀》《日本三代實錄》所載的戰況是研究八世紀日本的第一手材料，多賀城跡、志波古城跡、子鳥子遺跡等考古遺址則讓文字紀錄得到器物印證；蝦夷一詞從此成為正史處理北方異族的固定用語，其背後的邊疆想像一路影響到後世的北方政策與地名。
impactEn: This border war of thirty-eight years ended in tactical victory for the court, but it was paid for in institutional and financial terms. Its immediate consequence was the reorganization of the northeast: after the Isawa chiefs submitted in 802 the court established a garrison at Taga Castle, the provincial capital of Mutsu, consolidated the line of saku, brought the northern districts under uniform administration, and enrolled the chiefs who had submitted into the bureaucratic order with surnames and ranks, so that the Emishi groups moved from an independent tribal confederation towards being provincial subjects of the court; large numbers of hostages were also sent to the capital, and their descendants became one of the sources of the hostage kings and of the great northern houses. The location of the capital changed as a result of the war: Kanmu's move to Nagaoka in 784 is read as an evasion of the northern cavalry threat, and after the move to Heian-kyō in 794 the natural mountain barrier replaced the Mutsu line that had lain close at hand. Institutionally, the chōei taishōgun and the garrison system pioneered by Sakanoue no Tamuramaro were fixed, the management of Taga, the system of frontier posts and the tactics of horse archery all became the framework of Japan's northern defence for the three centuries that followed. For the historical record, the accounts in the Shoku Nihongi and the Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku are the primary sources for the eighth century, and sites such as Taga, Shiwa Castle and Konezako allow the written record to be checked against objects; the word Emishi became the fixed term of the official histories for the northern other, and the frontier imagination behind it ran on into later northern policy and place names.
result: 三八年戰爭在811年大致畫上句號：朝廷判定主要戰事已經結束，絕大多數蝦夷部族接受編戶與給姓，多賀城成為日本東北的軍政樞紐；802年降附的石城部首領阿多留威與モレ在803年被送往京師並遭處死，其部眾則留在原地成為朝廷的編戶。殘餘的抵抗並未立即消失：以石城、桃生為首的部分部族以及陸奧以北的地區仍保持相對獨立，811年後零星衝突依舊，顯示所謂平定只是把大範圍的部族聯盟戰爭壓縮成零星邊境衝突而已。從長期的勝負看，這是一場王朝的勝利：朝廷贏得了東北的稅源、鐵源與馬源，修復了首都與國府之間的通道，把北方邊防從臨時性遠征改為常設鎮守；代價則是數十年不斷的徵兵與遠程調度所造成的財政壓力，以及首都兩度遷徙與邊境線永久化之後的長期防務負擔。對蝦夷諸部而言，部族獨立的時代結束，取而代之的是王朝體系的編戶化與北方地方豪族的崛起，這批豪族最終在平安末年以藤原北方三家與安倍、清原的形態延續下去。作為三十八年拉鋸的紀念，戰爭留下的最大遺產是制度性的：以鎮守代替遠征的北方國防路線，就此在日本的邊疆史上定形。
resultEn: The Thirty-Eight Years' War was effectively closed in 811, when the court judged the main fighting to be over; the great majority of the Emishi groups accepted enrolment and the granting of surnames, and Taga Castle became the military and administrative pivot of northeastern Japan. The Isawa chiefs Aterui and More, who had submitted in 802, were brought to the capital in 803 and executed, while their people stayed on the ground as enrolled subjects. Resistance did not vanish at once: groups around the Isawa and the Momuse and the districts north of Mutsu remained relatively independent, and clashes continued after 811, showing that the pacification had only compressed a large-scale tribal conflict into scattered border incidents. In the long run this was a dynastic victory. The court won the taxes, the iron and the horses of the northeast, repaired the corridor between the capital and the provincial capital, and turned northern defence from episodic expeditions into standing garrison warfare; the price was the fiscal strain of three decades of continuous conscription and long-range deployment, together with two moves of the capital and the permanent burden of a fixed frontier line. For the Emishi groups, the age of tribal independence ended, replaced by enrolment into the dynastic system and by the rise of regional houses in the north, which later continued in the form of the northern three Fujiwara and the Abe and Seiwa lines at the end of the Heian period. The greatest legacy of thirty-eight years of hard fighting was institutional: the northern defence line based on standing garrisons rather than distant expeditions was fixed in the frontier history of Japan.
